thread:
Maya: FYI — ACME reported a regression after the INT8 profile rollout earlier today. They say answers became more 'assertive' and lost some structured fields in our JSON outputs. Also seeing intermittent 401s in their logs and an unexplained billing token spike. Putting details here so eng can triage.

Maya: Customer excerpt (redacted): 
- time: 2026-03-12T14:05Z
- observed: missing `entities` array in ~12% of completions, hallucinated URLs, confidence score changes
- other: several `401 Unauthorized` errors around 14:09-14:11, then high token usage for same prompts.

Maya: Repro steps they provided: 
1) POST to /v1/generate with model="redwood-xl-3b-int8"
2) prompt: "Extract contact fields from text and return JSON with keys name,email,phone"
3) got short answer, fields empty, then later received 401 on retry.

Alex: :eyes: marking P1 for now until we confirm blast radius. @Priya @Tom can you take a look? Any recent auth or billing infra changes rolled with the quant rollout?

Priya: Not to my knowledge on auth. We did push a new INT8 quant profile library at 14:00 with the rollout pipeline. It touched kernel selection and tokenization helpers for some models. I'll check the release diff.

Tom: Can we get one example where we have before/after outputs from the customer? Need exact prompt + two outputs (pre-quant/int8-off vs post-quant/int8-on). Also want full request/response headers (to check model variant & routing).

Maya: I asked for that and they sent this small pair (sanitized):
```
# pre (old): model=redwood-xl-3b, prompt=extract contact
{"name":"J. Doe","email":"j.doe@example.com","phone":"(555) 123-4567","entities":["contact"]}
# post (after INT8): model=redwood-xl-3b-int8, prompt=extract contact
{"name":"","email":"","phone":"","text":"we think this is John"}
```

Priya: Huh — empty fields suggests tokenization or tokenizer-vocab alignment issue. INT8 change shouldn't modify tokenizer but our new kernel hooks include a normalization pass that accidentally toggled a legacy token-splitter for certain punctuation. That could nudge decoding and prompt parsing.

Tom: That could explain missing structured fields (decoder output shifted). But what about the 401s and the billing spike? Could be unrelated timing overlap. @Alex any oncall logs for auth at 14:09?

Alex: Checking auth logs now. Quick summary: a burst of malformed auth headers from a single customer IP range at 14:08 triggered our short-lived rate-limited 401 path for a subset of requests. Appears to be client-side token refresh flapping. I don't see a platform-wide auth rollout. So auth error likely customer-specific concurrent with our rollout.

Sam: For billing spike — we saw a small uptick in tokens for a handful of tenants during the canary. Probably due to decoding differences producing longer outputs for certain prompts (e.g., verbose hallucinations). I'll correlate billing->model-variant mapping.

Priya: Plan: 1) Roll back the normalization patch from the INT8 library in the canary pool immediately. 2) Run targeted A/B on the customer's workload (if they consent) comparing old vs patched INT8. 3) Add a tokenizer-consistency unit test to prevent this regression.

Priya: @deploy-bot can you schedule a rollback of the INT8 patch from canary nodes in us-west-2? Keep it to canary assets only.

deploy-bot: Scheduled: rollback-int8-normalizer-canary at 1901112400. Estimated completion 5m. Notifying oncall.

Alex: I'll keep monitoring auth logs but nothing platform-wide to change.

Tom: I patched a quick repro locally — when the normalizer runs it rewrites some punctuation tokens (quotes, commas) into subtoken sequences. That changes the KV cache alignment and occasionally moves JSON bracket tokens across beam hypotheses. Reproduced inconsistent JSON keys in ~8% of runs with seed noise.

Tom: Short-term mitigation: pin the tokenizer behavior for INT8 profile to the stable tokenizer implementation (skip the new normalizer) and force the model to use deterministic decoding for structured-output routes. Priya can push a canary.

Priya: Pushing tokenizer-pin to canary now. Will also add a guard to avoid applying the normalizer to any model route with `response_schema` enabled.

Maya: I told ACME we'll run a targeted canary comparing their traffic against stable and share diffs. They asked for ETA — said it's blocking production.

Sam: ETA: canary change will be live in ~15 minutes after rollback completes. Then we'll capture 100 sample responses and compare. If they look good we'll proceed to full rollback of the INT8 normalizer.

Maya: Customer replied: appreciative, can we also get a bill correction if tokens spiked due to our rollout? They provided a CSV of requests around 14:05-14:15.

Sam: We'll scope the billing claim. If it's caused by our change we should refund or credit. Need product + finance signoff after we confirm causation.

Priya: Canary rollback finished at 1901112460. Starting A/B with pinned tokenizer.

Tom: Early results (50 samples): pinned -> fields present in 96% of responses. normalizer -> missing fields ~9%. Looks promising.

Maya: Sent update to customer with interim results and asked if they want us to proceed with full rollback. They said yes.

Priya: Filing rollback request for full INT8 normalizer from all pools. Will coordinate maintenance window if needed but aim for immediate rollback for affected customers.

Alex: I'll keep watching for any auth anomalies; remind customer to rotate tokens if they saw refresh errors.

Sam: I'll draft the billing credit proposal and loop in finance.

Maya: Thanks team. I'll keep the thread updated with customer acceptance and final notes. :thumbsup:

Maya: customer accepted rollback and validated samples at 1901112880 — fields restored. They requested a credit; sent to finance. Closing after billing confirmation.
